SPRINT 66 (V0.29.20) COMPLETE -- 7/7. US-497 (the IMU live-instrument card) DONE. No dev work remains; the next move is the PM's single on-Pi BENCH SESSION covering all 6 owed checks (US-494/495/496/498 render checks + US-478's live IMU read + US-497's card).
THE LESSON, and it generalises past this card: EVERY HONEST-AVAILABILITY PATTERN THIS PROJECT HAS BUILT ASSUMES ABSENCE IS VISIBLE ONCE RENDERED. A gray 'NA' tile reads as dead at a glance -- that is why US-429/US-496 work. A LIVE GRAPHICAL INSTRUMENT BREAKS THAT ASSUMPTION: a g-dot frozen at 0.4 g reads exactly like a car holding a steady corner. It is a FABRICATED MEASUREMENT, not a visible gap, and nothing about it looks wrong. So for any instrument with GEOMETRY, staleness must blank the geometry, not gray a label. Applied here: the idle path carries no geometry key at all and the renderer replaces the body wholesale (a stale <svg> left under an idle message IS the frozen instrument). Expect this again for any future gauge/needle/graph card.
AND THE INVERSE TRAP, which is just as easy to ship: A REAL 0.00 g READING IS LIVE, NOT ABSENT. A stationary car genuinely measures zero. Collapsing 'measured zero' into 'no reading' would blank a working instrument at every traffic light. Both directions are pinned by test.
GROUND A THRESHOLD TO ITS PRODUCER, AND DO NOT REUSE A CONSTANT JUST BECAUSE IT EXISTS. IMU_STALE_SEC=2.0 = 8 missed writes at the bridge's stateHz=4. I deliberately did NOT reuse the light card's 10s luxStaleSec: a 10s-old lux is still roughly true, a 10s-old g-vector is meaningless. Reaching for a nearby constant is how a threshold ends up governing a fact it was never measured against. FLAGGED as Rex-derived (with G_FULL_SCALE=1.0g, a DISPLAY scale not a vehicle limit -> Spool) exactly like US-478's tau.
A SIGN ERROR IN AN INSTRUMENT IS INVISIBLE IN A SCREENSHOT -- it only shows to a human in a moving car. Two defenses worth copying: pin the SCREEN-COORDINATE conversion by test (gLon+ = accelerating -> NEGATIVE y is where the mistake lives), and PUT THE CONTRACT IN WORDS ON THE CARD ('0.30 right - 0.12 brake') so a backwards mount is obvious at the bench instead of a silently mirrored dot. That text is now the on-Pi diagnostic for US-478's owed mount check.
CLAMP DIRECTIONALLY, NEVER PER-AXIS: clamping x and y independently swings an over-scale diagonal to the CORNER and misreports which way the car was loaded. Scale the whole vector. And FLAG the clamp (amber dot) while the tile keeps the true magnitude -- a silent clamp renders a 1.4 g stop as a tidy 1.0 g one.

THE ONE REAL DESIGN PROBLEM, and the AC makes it sound mechanical: AN ACCELEROMETER CANNOT TELL GRAVITY FROM ACCELERATION. Publish the raw horizontal components and a board bolted in at 10 degrees pins a PERMANENT PHANTOM 0.17 g on the g-meter, parked, forever. And the obvious fix is MATHEMATICALLY EMPTY: rotate the measured vector onto 'up' and subtract its own magnitude and the horizontal residual is IDENTICALLY ZERO by construction -- it looks right, tests green against a hand-built fixture, and reads zero on a real drive. The answer is a slow low-pass GRAVITY REFERENCE (tau=5s) whose fast residual is the g-meter. Work the physics before writing the bridge; this one would have shipped silently wrong.
DERIVE A SHARED PHYSICAL FACT ONCE. That same gravity estimate defines the level frame (gLat/gLon), the pitch (gradePct) AND the heading tilt-compensation. Three derivations = three chances for the compass and the grade to disagree about which way is down.
GROUND CADENCE TO THE CONSUMER: IMU bursts at 50 Hz, carousel.js POLL_MS=250, so stateHz=4 is the entire observable budget -- everything above it is tmpfs churn nobody can see. And say which numbers are NOT grounded: tau=5.0 is a Rex-derived filter constant, config-parameterized and FLAGGED to Atlas/Spool for confirmation against a real drive. stateHz is grounded; tau is not; both are in the notes as such.
A STATE CHANGE MUST BYPASS THE RATE LIMIT: the absent-sensor write skips the decimation window, because rate-limiting it would leave the last live g reading on the card looking current -- the rate limiter would have manufactured a frozen instrument. Same family as the stale-mag rule (a frozen compass needle is worse than an absent one).
FOR US-497 (next): the card is a PURE CONSUMER -- no fusion, no re-derivation. Sign contract is gLon + = accelerating / - = braking, gLat + = RIGHT, gradePct + = climbing, headingDeg MAGNETIC not true. altitude is ALWAYS null with reasons.altitude='no_source'. Absent/stale ts -> idle card. The `reasons` map is the per-field gray vocabulary: sensor_absent / no_mag_reading / tilt_unresolved / pitch_out_of_range / no_source. Full contract table is in specs/architecture.md 10.8.2 -- build the fixture from THAT, not from my test file.
CONFIG: pi.sensors.imu.enabled flipped TRUE (first run of the IMU reader), so edr_imu_sample rows now land at persistHz=25 alongside the light rows -- worth one df check at the bench.

THE HEADLINE LESSON: TO CATCH A COMPOSITION BUG, SPLIT THE HARNESS ALONG THE SEAM THE BUG CROSSED. All three defects this sprint fixed had one shape -- every part tested green and the composition was broken (S1: a dependency the entry point never injected, computeBootState was always right; S2: correct JS defeated by a stylesheet the JS cannot see; S5: three valid CSS declarations interacting to a black screen). So the backstop is TWO PROCESSES THAT CANNOT SEE EACH OTHER'S VERDICT: node runs the SHIPPED carousel.js / boot-state-poll.js against a mini-DOM and dumps the attributes (it knows nothing about CSS); Python resolves the SHIPPED stylesheet over that DOM and answers the only question that matters -- does this element have a box. Neither half can launder the other's answer. That property is what every existing UI test lacked.
THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL, and it generalises to any DOM harness: IDL properties must REFLECT to CONTENT ATTRIBUTES. `el.hidden = true` has to land as the `hidden` ATTRIBUTE, because the attribute is what the cascade selects on. A harness storing it as a private flag would have reproduced US-495's BLIND SPOT and passed the broken stylesheet without a murmur. Everything else in mini_dom.js is scoped to the ~15 DOM methods the kits actually touch -- enumerated from the source with grep, not guessed. It is not a jsdom clone and must not grow into one.
PROVEN RED AGAINST REAL HISTORY, not asserted: `git show <fixcommit>^:<path>` gives you the actual defective artifact, and a stdlib-only module can be loaded LIVE via importlib and run. THE HEADLINE LESSON: REVERSING AN ANIMATION IS TWO REVERSALS, AND SHIPPING ONE OF THEM IS A BLACK SCREEN. The kit flipped `animation-direction: reverse` on every class with a comment saying 'the keyframes are symmetric enough that reverse just works'. Direction was the easy half; the running ORDER also has to reverse. The boot timeline ENDS with a fadeout DELAYED 6s, and `animation-fill-mode: both` holds the reversed animation's FIRST RELEVANT keyframe through that delay -- which for direction:reverse is `to`, i.e. opacity 0. So the fill-mode that exists to prevent a flash of unstyled content pinned the mark invisible for 6 seconds of a 7-SECOND GRACE WINDOW (pi.powerWatch.smoothingSec): black for essentially the whole shutdown. Fix = reversed delay is T - (bootDelay + bootDuration), T = 6.5s; derived from splash.svg, no invented numbers, and the test RE-DERIVES them so re-timing the boot re-aims the closeout.
NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE BUG, because it will recur: three individually-correct declarations (a delay, a fill-mode, a direction) interacting. Every part had a passing test. Every surrounding component worked -- sequencer emitted, emitter wrote, .path watched the right file, server served the right page with the token, JS revealed the stage on time. The surface it revealed was black. When a UI 'does nothing' and all the parts test green, stop testing parts and start SAMPLING THE OUTPUT ON A CLOCK.
SO THAT IS WHAT THE TEST DOES: tests/ui/test_shutdown_splash_render.py resolves the shipped CSS (cascade + !important, comma-list shorthands, fill-mode/direction/delay) and samples the mark's opacity every 250ms across the real grace window read from config. RED naming every blank instant t=[1.0..6.0]. One assertion I wrote OVER-CLAIMED -- 'brightness never rises' failed on the DESIGNED throb, whose recovery genuinely raises brightness -- and I corrected the test to the honest envelope claim (max->low endpoints, second half never brighter than the first) rather than keeping a green-looking lie. Fidelity limit is stated in the file: easings treated as linear, so endpoints and the SIGN of a change are exact, mid-segment values are not; every assertion is zero-vs-nonzero or an endpoint.
A KEEP-LIST IS A COST, NOT A SAFETY NET -- the deploy half, and it generalises. US-495 keep-listed the closeout surface as 'the kit's install.sh owns those'. But a keep-listed asset is never installed, never pruned and never byte-verified; its only refresh path was the A-9 kiosk step, which is ALLOWED TO WARN AND SKIP (install.sh aborts if it cannot detect session type or chromium). So the stale hole US-495 closed for boot was still open for shutdown -- where it only shows itself DURING a shutdown, nobody watching, no re-run. Moved the whole surface into the manifest (both installers copy identical bytes from the same synced kit, so ownership costs nothing and buys the verify). Keep-list is now version.txt alone, which earns it: the deploy GENERATES it, so the manifest cannot name it. Ask of any keep-list entry: who verifies this, and are they allowed to skip?
